comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Handoff from a second (epic-driver) session that was working this story in parallel and is now STANDING DOWN — this ticket is yours. Posting findings + a harvestable patch so none of it has to be rediscovered.

## Three content-DESTROYING pandoc behaviours a real-prose corpus caught
All measured on pandoc 3.6.1 (the binary bundled in the `pypandoc-binary==1.15` wheel), rendering `-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`. Each one silently corrupts content, and none is visible from hand-written examples:

1. **pandoc escapes punctuation INSIDE code spans.** `` `-> <- <-> =>` `` renders as `{{\-> <\- <-> =>}}`. Pre-substituting arrows correctly spares code, and pandoc corrupts it anyway on the way out. A "skip code when substituting" rule alone is NOT sufficient.
2. **pandoc DELETES HTML comments.** A lone `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` renders to the EMPTY STRING. That is rebar's own reconciler echo marker, so this is a correctness bug, not a cosmetic one — a dropped marker breaks loop-breaking.
3. **A naive arrow rule corrupts the HTML-comment terminator.** `-->` contains `->`, so substitution rewrites it to `-→`. Fix: match `<!--` and `-->` FIRST and map them to themselves so the inner arrow is consumed by the delimiter.

Mitigation that covers all three without enumerating pandoc's quirks: a **post-render code-preservation check** — after converting a unit, require every code fragment of the source to appear verbatim in the output, else fall back to that unit's original Markdown. This converts unpredictable escaping into a safe fallback. Recommend adding it whatever the implementation shape.

Also worth keeping: pandoc's jira writer emits a stray `{anchor:}` after EVERY heading (`h1. {anchor:}Title`) — it is not content and needs stripping; and re-rendering already-wiki text as Markdown is destructive (`{{x}}` → `\{\{x\}\}`, `{noformat}` dissolves), so a unit that already looks like wiki should pass through.

## Harvestable implementation: /tmp/pony-swan-271c.patch
Complete, gates-green, NOT pushed and NOT committed anywhere. 10 files / ~1,010 insertions:
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (318 LOC) — segmenting renderer: blank-line/fence-aware split, safe/table/verbatim classification, code-aware arrow substitution, `{noformat}` table wrap, `{anchor:}` strip, post-render code-preservation check, already-wiki passthrough, identity fallback when pandoc is absent.
- `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py` + `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` — deterministic generator and a scrubbed 178-body fixture (29 code-arrow / 29 table / 120 prose), every shard <=127 KB.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render.py` + `test_wiki_render_corpus.py` — 57 tests passing.
- `pyproject.toml` `wiki` extra (`pypandoc-binary==1.15`, pinned exactly) + dev pin so CI actually exercises the path; registered in `src/rebar/_optional.py`.
- `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` — the vocabulary gate scans fixture CONTENT and fails on historical ticket prose, so the fixture directory needs excluding (it is captured data, not authored text). Expect this failure otherwise.

Measured over that fixture: 92.7% of bodies and 98.4% of characters render rich; 0 code-arrow fragments lost; 31/31 table bodies still tables; all HTML comments survive. `make lint` and `make typecheck` both green; `wiki_render.py` is 318 LOC (inside the 200-500 target, under the 800 cap).

Apologies for the earlier plan-material churn — a description edit of mine landed and was superseded by yours; that session is now stood down and will make no further edits here.

# DC segmenting Markdown-to-wiki renderer

## Problem
DC stores wiki while rebar authors Markdown and sends Markdown literally. Whole-body pandoc 3.6.1 escapes arrows, erodes tables, and deletes `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->`.

Add an unwired pure renderer. `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` retains 32,767-character truncation; its other methods, `OutboundFieldMapper`, CREATE, `normalize_rich_text`, and live sends stay unchanged. Story 3388 owns cutover/echo/codec convergence; 5c0e owns timeout/process/GPL/SBOM hardening.

Pandoc's maintained pair produced 98.4% eligible-character coverage; md-to-jira, mistune-jira, and md-jira lack equivalent fidelity. ADR 0083 governs imports. ADR 0095 plus `.numbers/0095` records invariants, pin provenance, alternatives, platform, and deferrals.

## Corpus
Commit a deterministic, fixed-seed scrubbed sample from `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py`: 29 code-arrow, 29 table, 120 prose (178); shards below 500 KB. Per-stratum targets are PINNED so a growing store cannot silently change the corpus. Change `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py`'s filter to skip `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`; the scrub also maps vocabulary other repo-wide guards reject (retired bridge spellings, `--force-close`). Reject emails, tenant hostnames, URLs.

Eligible means a classifier-6 unit dispatched to pandoc. Body ratio = bodies whose rendering changed / 178; character ratio = characters of changed bodies / all corpus characters. Measuring characters over ELIGIBLE-UNIT source instead is unachievable: 98,214 of 296,511 eligible characters are unmarked prose pandoc returns byte-identical, capping it at 0.669. Pin measured 0.916/0.969; require >=0.90/>=0.95 plus a non-vacuous dispatched-and-changed check.

## Renderer contract
Add `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` with `render_markdown_to_wiki(markdown: str) -> str`.

Two-phase left-to-right lexer:
1. Lock complete `{noformat}` spans, HTML comments from `<!--` through the next `-->`, backtick/tilde fences, and four-space-indented blocks, including internal blank lines. Locked HTML comment spans pass exactly even when adjacent to prose.
2. Split intervening text into blank-line blocks plus list items; preserve separators/order.

Classify, in order:
1. Locked blocks and units beginning `h1.`-`h6.`, `{code}`, or `{noformat}` pass exactly.
2. An inline-Jira scanner masks code, then recognizes `[label|target]`, `{color:name}...{color}`, and `{{monospace}}` as UNAMBIGUOUS (these settle a unit alone, even inside a bullet), and `*strong*` (never `**`) / `_emphasis_` as AMBIGUOUS (they settle only a unit with no CommonMark-only heading/quote/list/fence/backtick/`**`/image/`[label](target)`). Without that split a rendered bullet re-renders and oscillates. ADR records the tradeoff.
3. ASCII table = >=2 pipe-bearing lines with a pipes/colons/hyphens/whitespace delimiter row. Wrap exact bytes once in `{noformat}`.
4. HTML tag matching `<[/!]?[A-Za-z][^>]*>` passes exactly; HTML comments were already locked in phase 1.
5. Prose outside extracted code containing `(?`, `\b`, `\d`, `\s`, `\w`, or a bracket class followed by `*`, `+`, `?`, or `{n,m}` passes exactly.
6. Remaining headings, quotes, list items, and prose render via pypandoc `commonmark -> jira` with `--wrap=none`.

Code fragments are fences, four-space blocks, and inline spans with matching backtick runs; mask them before classifiers and arrows. One regex pass ordered `<!--`, `-->`, `<->`, `->`, `<-`, `=>` maps arrows to ↔/→/←/⇒ and delimiters to themselves. Inline code copies exactly.

Every extracted fragment must appear byte-identically in order after conversion or that unit falls back. Strip content-free `{anchor:}` after headings. Five-pass tests start from Markdown and prove passes 2-5 byte-identical. Use real pandoc outputs for bold, italic, links, and monospace; NO monkeypatch anywhere. A probe observed `*b*`, `_i_`, `[l|http://x]`, and `` `mono` `` -> `{{mono}}`, so monospace needs no synthetic shape. The same probe established the jira writer NEVER emits `{color:...}` (a color span is stripped to plain text under both readers), so color is not a pandoc output to pin -- it is only pre-existing markup the inline scanner passes exactly, covered by the pre-existing-wiki fixtures.

Missing pypandoc returns the body and warns `wiki_render_fallback` with only `reason="pandoc_absent"`; conversion/preservation failure returns the unit and debugs the same event with `"conversion_failure"`/`"preservation_failure"`. Never log bodies. Module state is immutable.

## Dependency/CI
Add `wiki = ["pypandoc-binary==1.15"]` plus wiki in dev, register its pypandoc probe, and lock. Optionality adds `wiki:wiki`, removes stale `eval:eval`, and changes the union to `agents,tracing,wiki`. Dynamic tests `test_optionality_loop_covers_every_declared_extra` and `test_eval_extra_is_gone` plus full suite prove parity.

A clean-environment probe established `pypandoc.__version__ == 1.15`, pandoc `3.6.1`, `# Heading` → `h1. {anchor:}Heading\n`, `` `mono` `` → `{{mono}}\n`, and no `{color:...}` form; ADR 0095 records that provenance. A non-skipping test hard-imports pypandoc and asserts those exact values. It gates Linux/macOS CI; Windows wheels exist, and a platform without one falls back to identity. Wiki tests never importorskip.

Changed paths: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py`; `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py`; `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`; `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render.py`; `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py`; `pyproject.toml`; `uv.lock`; `src/rebar/_optional.py`; `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`; `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py`; `docs/adr/0095-dc-segmenting-wiki-renderer.md`; `docs/adr/.numbers/0095`.

## Verification
Author the oracle RED-first without skip/xfail. Run `make lint`/`make typecheck`/`make test` with worktree `.venv` on PATH. Stateless: no store/retry/cache contention.

CLI/MCP/API/facade: out of scope, this is unwired. Dual direction: story 3388. Cloud: ADF child.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Classifier-6 units render through real pandoc in order; `test_dc_segmenting_passthrough`.
- [ ] Tables preserve exact bytes once; table passthrough and five-pass tests.
- [ ] HTML/regex-dangerous units preserve exact bytes; passthrough tests.
- [ ] Specified arrows convert prose; `test_arrow_substitution_cases`.
- [ ] Code arrows and prose/code `-->` stay exact; arrow tests.
- [ ] 29 code-arrow fixtures retain protected excerpts; corpus test.
- [ ] 29 tables keep exact bytes inside one noformat wrapper over five passes.
- [ ] HTML comments survive exactly; corpus HTML test.
- [ ] Block and inline Jira forms stay byte-identical for five passes.
- [ ] Real-pandoc bold/italic/link/monospace outputs stabilize after pass one.
- [ ] Pre-existing `{color:name}` markup passes exactly; pandoc emits no color form.
- [ ] Missing pandoc returns exact body and content-free `wiki_render_fallback:pandoc_absent`.
- [ ] Conversion failure returns exact unit and logs only `conversion_failure`.
- [ ] Preservation failure returns exact unit and logs only `preservation_failure`.
- [ ] wiki locks pypandoc-binary 1.15; packaging test.
- [ ] wiki installs alone and jointly without eval; uv sync and optionality lane.
- [ ] Real binary reports pandoc 3.6.1; non-skipping pin test.
- [ ] Real jira heading conversion equals `h1. {anchor:}Heading\n`; pin test.
- [ ] Body ratio >=0.90 and character ratio >=0.95, with eligible units dispatched and changed.
- [ ] Cardinality is 29+29+120=178; pinned cardinality test.
- [ ] Fixtures contain no email, tenant hostname, or URL; secrets test.
- [ ] Heading output has no content-free anchor; passthrough test.
- [ ] ADR marker passes `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`.
- [ ] ADR has Decision/Invariants/Pin/Alternatives/Platform/Deferrals; ADR test.
- [ ] Existing WikiTextCodec tests stay unmodified; full suite.
